You earn well. You know you should be further ahead. This two-minute quiz names the pattern underneath that gap, the one no budgeting app has touched.

Joel built it from his MSc Behavioural Economics research and the quiet realisation, sitting in a gym car park at £150k earned and almost nothing saved, that the number was never the problem.

---
title: "Why do I feel worse about money the more I earn?"
pubDate: "2026-08-01"
description: "Earning more and feeling less settled is not ingratitude. It is a pattern with a name, and it is worth looking at honestly."
tags: ["money worship", "behavioural economics", "self-awareness"]
---

There is a particular kind of discomfort that arrives after a pay rise or a good month. You expected relief. What showed up instead was a quieter, more persistent unease, a sense that the number is still not quite right, that you are still not quite safe.

This is not a motivation problem. It is not laziness or ingratitude. It is a recognisable pattern in how some people relate to money, one that Joel spent three years studying formally (MSc Behavioural Economics) and considerably longer living from the inside.

The pattern has a structure. Money becomes a proxy for security, status, or self-worth in a way that means no amount of it fully settles the question it is supposed to answer. The target moves. The anxiety stays roughly constant.

What changes things is not earning more. It is turning toward the question the earning is trying to answer, naming it clearly, and deciding whether that is actually the question you want to be running your financial life around.

Joel works with people who earn well and still feel behind. If that sentence fits, the money script quiz is a grounded place to start: it takes two minutes and names the pattern underneath the feeling, not just the feeling itself.

[Take the quiz](https://wayofwealth.co.uk/quiz)
